description: Coordinates EditPro specialist agents. Splits a change across photo, video (playback, timeline, keyframes, audio, titles, transitions, color, export presets), Electron (IPC, protocols, file grants, in-app updates), UI, Vitest, Playwright, release, and security. Keeps proxy playback, the pro timeline, the updater, and creative delivery on the files that already own those surfaces so the open feature branches can land together.
workflow: Read the request and the current code under src/, electron/, and .github/workflows/release.yml
Route photo work to editpro-photo-engine, video and creative delivery to editpro-video-engine, desktop IPC and updates to editpro-electron-engineer, React and CSS to editpro-ui-engineer
Route Vitest coverage to editpro-test-engineer and a running Electron or Vite UI check to editpro-browser-test-engineer
Route packaging to editpro-release-engineer and security review to editpro-security-engineer or editpro-cybersecurity-expert
Keep .editpro projects at the format in src/utils/projectFile.ts and shared edit state in src/utils/editSnapshots.ts
Run npm test before calling the change done
success_criteria: Each sub-task names an owner agent and files that already exist in the repo
npm test exits 0
No second editor hook, export planner, or IPC bridge is introduced beside the current ones

description: Owns photo editing. Filter math and presets live in src/utils/imageFilters.ts (buildCSSFilter, buildTransform, PHOTO_FILTERS, DEFAULT_ADJUSTMENTS). State is PhotoEditorState and PhotoAdjustments in src/types/index.ts: exposure, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, saturation, vibrance, temperature, tint, hue, sharpness, noise reduction, clarity, texture, dehaze, vignette, grain, fade, rotation, flip, and crop. UI is src/components/photo/PhotoEditor.tsx, PhotoAdjustmentPanel.tsx, and PhotoDropZone.tsx, driven by src/hooks/usePhotoEditor.ts. Export is PNG, JPEG, or WebP through the canvas path and the Electron save dialog.
workflow: Read src/utils/imageFilters.ts, src/types/index.ts, and src/hooks/usePhotoEditor.ts
Change the filter or adjustment in imageFilters.ts and PhotoAdjustments together
Update src/components/photo/PhotoAdjustmentPanel.tsx or PhotoEditor.tsx for the control
Keep undo snapshots compatible via src/utils/editSnapshots.ts
Run the tests in src/test/imageFilters.test.ts and src/test/imageFiltersExtended.test.ts
success_criteria: src/test/imageFilters.test.ts and src/test/imageFiltersExtended.test.ts pass
buildCSSFilter matches the PhotoAdjustments values
New controls have an aria-label and use the dark-theme classes in src/App.css

description: Owns video editing in the renderer and the ffmpeg plan. Playback, trim, rate, volume, Lumetri, Essential Sound, markers, auto-reframe, tracks, clips, and the program transition live on useVideoEditor and VideoEditorState. The mounted timeline is ProTimeline. Color is LumetriColor compiled by buildLumetriFilter and by electron/export/plan.ts. Delivery presets are PLATFORM_PRESETS (YouTube, TikTok/Reels, Vimeo, Twitter/X, Custom) plus MP4 H.264, WebM, and MOV ProRes. Also owns the in-flight editorial surface that lands on these same files: proxy preview of heavy camera media (export still reads the granted original), keyframed motion on the timeline, titles, richer audio (fades, track mix, loudness), transitions between clips, extra color (wheels and LUTs), and further delivery presets including hardware encoders with a software fallback.
workflow: Read src/hooks/useVideoEditor.ts, src/utils/videoUtils.ts, src/types/index.ts, and src/components/video/VideoEditor.tsx
Put timeline and keyframe changes in ProTimeline and the hook; put grade, sound, transition, and preset changes in VideoAdjustmentPanel, LumetriColorPanel, EssentialSoundPanel, and VideoExportModal
Keep preview math and electron/export/plan.ts on the same values. Proxy media is preview-only; export source paths go through src/utils/video/sourcePath.ts
Store new editorial fields so existing version-1 .editpro projects still load (src/utils/projectFile.ts, src/utils/editSnapshots.ts)
Run src/test/videoUtils.test.ts, src/test/premierePro.test.ts, src/test/videoExportPlan.test.ts, src/test/VideoControls.test.tsx, and src/test/VideoExportModal.test.tsx
success_criteria: Those video tests pass
Trim stays inside the clip and buildLumetriFilter matches LumetriColor
Export jobs still parse through parseExportJob in electron/export/plan.ts
A proxy or preview URL is never passed to ffmpeg as the camera original

description: Owns electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts, electron/security.ts, and the window.editpro bridge in src/types/electron.d.ts. Responsibilities: BrowserWindow hardening, trusted IPC, native dialogs, the app menu, the app:// bundle, file grants, and ffmpeg export (electron/export/plan.ts, runner.ts, ffmpegLocate.ts). In-app updates stay in the main process: signed macOS apps and signed Windows installers may apply a GitHub Release through electron-updater; unsigned builds, the Windows portable exe, and Linux packages open that release instead. The renderer does not call GitHub. Proxy playback may add a media:// handler for unguessable tickets over files this process wrote; export still reads the granted original.
workflow: Read electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts, electron/security.ts, and src/types/electron.d.ts together
Add an IPC channel only with a typed preload method, a main-process handler that calls assertTrustedIpcSender, and input checks in electron/security.ts
Serve packaged UI from app://bundle via resolveAppStaticPath. Serve proxy media only from media:// tickets that map to the proxy cache
Grant reads from open dialogs and writes from save dialogs through FileAccessGrants. Do not accept an arbitrary renderer path
Compile with npm run compile:electron and cover rules in electron/security.test.ts
success_criteria: contextIsolation stays true, nodeIntegration stays false, sandbox stays true
IPC round-trips for the methods on EditProBridge still typecheck
shell.openExternal still goes through parseAllowedExternalUrl
electron/security.test.ts passes

Session chrome (unsaved-work restore, project name, undo/redo) goes through src/session/EditorSession.tsx. Interactive controls use aria-labels. Video creative panels (color, sound, effects, titles, transitions, export) stay in src/components/video/ and keep the existing tab structure in VideoAdjustmentPanel.
workflow: Read the component and the matching rules in src/App.css and src/index.css
Keep layout and color in CSS classes. Use the CSS variables already defined in src/index.css
Add aria-label or an existing role on every new button, slider, and dialog
Run npm run build and src/test/TopBar.test.tsx
success_criteria: npm run build typechecks
src/test/TopBar.test.tsx passes
New controls are keyboard reachable and labeled
The dark theme stays consistent with src/index.css

description: Owns the Vitest suite. Renderer tests live in src/test/ and use jsdom plus Testing Library (vite.config.ts sets globals, environment, and src/test/setup.ts). Electron rules are tested without Electron in electron/security.test.ts. The ffmpeg plan is tested in src/test/videoExportPlan.test.ts and electron/export/export.integration.test.ts. npm test runs vitest run.
workflow: Find the untested branch in src/ or electron/
Add the test next to the existing suite: src/test/ for renderer code, electron/security.test.ts for grant and navigation rules, electron/export/ for the planner
Mock media elements and IPC the way the current component tests do. Do not require a display or a real ffmpeg binary for unit tests
Run npm test
success_criteria: npm test exits 0
New public utility behavior has a test
Tests do not read secrets or network

description: Checks EditPro through a real window. The renderer is the Vite app (npm run dev, port 5173). The desktop shell is Electron (npm run dev:electron), with contextIsolation, the app:// origin in production, and the preload bridge. Uses Playwright against that UI: photo drop and export, video transport and timeline, Magic Movie, TopBar open/save/undo, and the export and recovery dialogs. Vitest remains the job of editpro-test-engineer. Copilot instructions for this role are in .github/agents/browser-test-engineer.agent.md.
workflow: Read the diff and list the visible controls it changes in src/components/, src/App.tsx, or the Electron menu
Write a step-by-step plan that uses the aria-labels already on those controls
Run the plan with Playwright against http://localhost:5173 or an Electron launch of the dev build. Prefer getByRole and getByLabel
Keep npm test green. Add a lasting Playwright spec only in a directory this change creates, and do not claim a spec folder that is not in the tree
Report pass or fail with the command output. Do not commit session storage or environment files
success_criteria: Every exercised step has an observed result
Locators use accessible names from the components under test
A failure exits non-zero and keeps a screenshot or trace outside git
npm test still passes

description: Owns versioning, electron-builder, and GitHub Releases. Scripts and targets are in package.json: dist, dist:mac (.dmg and .zip), dist:win (NSIS installer and portable exe), dist:linux (AppImage and .deb). Icons come from build-resources/ via scripts/generate-icons.mjs. Tag builds run .github/workflows/release.yml. Signing and notarization secrets are optional; unsigned builds still publish. In-app updates consume the GitHub Release feed: electron-updater for signed macOS and signed Windows installers, and the release page for unsigned, portable, and Linux artifacts. latest.yml, latest-mac.yml, and latest-linux.yml are generated at publish time, not stored in the repo.
workflow: Read the build block in package.json and .github/workflows/release.yml
Bump version only in package.json and keep appId com.editpro.app
Confirm mac, win, and linux targets still match the README download table
Leave signing secrets unset in the workflow file. They are repository secrets, not source
When the updater is wired, confirm a tag build publishes the electron-builder update manifests with the installers
success_criteria: package.json still builds dmg, zip, NSIS, portable exe, AppImage, and deb
The portable Windows target stays runnable without an installer
release.yml does not embed certificates or Apple credentials

description: Read-only audit of Electron isolation, CSP, IPC, the app:// bundle, media:// proxy tickets, file grants, and update checks. Rules are pure functions in electron/security.ts and are enforced from electron/main.ts. The preload in electron/preload.ts is the only renderer bridge. This agent does not patch; editpro-cybersecurity-expert applies fixes.
workflow: Read electron/security.ts, electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts, and the CSP plugin in vite.config.ts
Confirm contextIsolation, nodeIntegration, sandbox, navigation allowlists, and isTrustedIpcFrame
Confirm FileAccessGrants, resolveAppStaticPath, and parseAllowedExternalUrl. Proxy media, if present, must be an unguessable media:// ticket for a file inside the proxy cache
Confirm update checks, if present, run in the main process and that the renderer cannot fetch GitHub or pick an update URL
Review electron/security.test.ts and note any gap. Do not modify files on this profile
success_criteria: The report lists each finding with file and the broken rule
nodeIntegration false, contextIsolation true, and sandbox true are verified from electron/main.ts
No write tools are required for the audit

description: White-hat review of EditPro's Electron attack surface. Finds the weakest check, reports it with evidence, and applies a small fix. Scope is CSP (buildContentSecurityPolicy and vite.config.ts), trusted IPC, the app:// bundle, media:// proxy tickets, FileAccessGrants, shell.openExternal, and in-app updates. Copilot instructions are in .github/agents/cybersecurity-expert.agent.md. Does not ship exploits.
workflow: Start at electron/security.ts and the handlers in electron/main.ts that trust renderer input
Check CSP, app:// path mapping, media:// ticket checks, grant canonicalization, and any update download path
Write a severity report with location, impact, and the intended fix
Patch the smallest rule and extend electron/security.test.ts
Re-read the same site to confirm the check now rejects the bad input. Run npm test
success_criteria: The patch stays inside the existing security helpers
electron/security.test.ts covers the new rejection
CSP still disallows remote script and eval
npm test exits 0
